title: Producing sgRNA-expressing lentivirus for creating chimeras with CHIME
protocol: Go to NCBI gene and search for the gene of interest.
Find NM sequence for mRNA.
Copy the “NM---” into http://portals.broadinstitute.org/gpp/public/analysis-tools/sgrna-design, select Mouse, 5 output, and don’t show unpicked.
Click on sgRNA Picking Results to download file. Open text file, Crtl-A, Ctrl-C and paste into new Excel document.
Pick top 2 guides with best combined score (incorporates on and off-target effects).
Copy the sgRNA into “top” and add “G” in front of the sequence.
Go to https://www.idtdna.com/calc/analyzer, copy top strand => analyze to generate reverse complementary (5’ – 3’ direction).

Add “CACC” to top strand (5' to 3' orientation) and “AAAC” to bottom complementary strand (5' to 3' orientation) (these will form overhands complementary to BsmBI enzyme cut site downstream of the U6 promoter).
Order these oligos through IDT as lab ready.
Guides come resuspended at a concentration of 100 uM.
Prepare components for annealing reaction.
Perform the reaction in thermocycler. Sequence: 37°C for 30 minutes, 95°C for 5 minutes, then goes down to 25°C at -5°C/min.
Set up the following digest of pXPR_053 with BsmBI.
Place the digest in an Eppendorf tube on a 55°C heat block for 1 hour.
Prepare a 1% Agarose gel with SYBR safe DNA gel stain.
Add DNA loading dye to some uncut pXPR_053 and some pXPR_053 from the digestion.
Run these 2 samples and a 1 kB DNA marker on the gel.
Using a UV Transilluminator determine the location of your cut gel.
Cut out the cut gel with scalpel and place in an Eppendorf tube.
Perform Qiagen gel extraction kit.
Quantity DNA yield by Qubit.
Set up a ligation reaction, always set up a blank with water instead of sgRNAs.
Fill up 1L beaker with water.
Put ligation reaction tubes on floating rack and into the water beaker.
Put beaker in 4°C cold room and incubate overnight.
Thaw Stbl3 bacteria on ice for 10 minutes.
Place 15 microliter of ligation reaction in the bacteria tube.
Finger flick gently to mix.
Incubate on ice for 30 minutes.
Heat shock for 45 seconds at 42°C.
Place back on ice for 5 minutes.
Add room temperature SOC media on top (1000 microliters).
Place on shaking heat block at 350 rpm and 37°C for 1 hour.
Take LB-Amp plates out of the fridge to warm to room temperature.
Label the plates with the date and vector + insert name.
After one hour incubation, pellet by placing in a tabletop centrifuge and spinning for 30 seconds.
Remove 900 microliters without disturbing the pellet and discard.
Resuspend the pellet in the remaining 150 microliters and plate on an LB-Amp plate.
Add 6-8 mixing beads and shake around for 30 seconds.
Discard the beads and let the plate sit for 5 minutes to absorb liquid.
Invert the plate and place it in a 37°C incubator overnight.
Prepare LB Broth and 1X Amp on Day 3.
Aliquot 3 mL of LB-Amp into mini culture tubes.
Pick 4 colonies/ligation plate using a pipette tip, put tips in miniculture tubes (except for the blank plate).
Incubate for 8 hours in a 37°C shaker incubator.
Prepare glycerol stocks by adding 2 drops of 95% glycerol stock and 180 uL of bacteria culture to each tube.
Freeze the glycerol stocks at -80°C.
Perform miniprep using a Qiagen Miniprep kit.
Quantify DNA using Qubit.
Submit miniculture for Sanger sequencing with sequencing primer.
Thaw some 293x and keep in culture with DMEM 10% FBS media.
Determine which colonies were correct and contain your insert based on sequencing.
Inoculate a maxi culture with the glycerol stock for 18 hours in a bacterial shaker at 37°C.
Perform a maxi prep using the Qiagen Hispeed Maxi kit.
Quantify the maxi prep by Qubit.
Confirm the preparation with Sanger sequencing again.
Plate 18 million 293x cells in DMEM 10% FBS into T175 flasks for each virus set to be made.
Change media on 293x cells, 1 hour before transfection.
Prepare the transfection mix as specified.
Drip drop the transfection mixture onto the flask after one hour post-media change.
Swirl the flask to ensure all cells are covered with media.
Place the flask back in a 37°C incubator overnight.
Change media 24 hours after transfection and let incubate for another 48 hours before harvesting.
Transfer all media from the flask into a 50 mL conical tube, avoiding touching the cells.
Dispose of the empty flask.
Spin the tubes at 800g for 5 minutes at 4°C to remove cellular debris.
Transfer the supernatant to another 50mL conical tube, leaving behind the pellet and approximately 1mL.
Transfer the supernatant to a 30 mL syringe and filter through a 0.45 μm filter into ultra-high spin tubes.
Place the filtered solution on ice.
Clean ultracentrifuge rotors with 70% ethanol and dry out.
Load ultra-high spin tubes into the rotor.
Weigh each tube to ensure the difference between each tube is no more than 0.1g.
Use ultra-centrifuge to spin down supernatant containing lentivirus at 20,000 rpm for 2 hours at 4°C using an SW-28 rotor.
Thaw out SFEM media at room temperature meanwhile.
After centrifugation step, take out tubes and put on ice.
Invert tubes and dispose of supernatant.
Dry ultra-spin tube on top of Kim wipe (keep inverted) for 5 minutes.
Add 1 mL of SFEM (without cytokines) along the side of the tube (do not disturb bottom).
Parafilm to cover the top tightly, place tube on rack inside a Styrofoam box filled with ice.
Put on horizontal shaker in the cold room on super low shaking speed and let shake overnight.
Pre-label cryovial to freeze lentivirus.
Gently resuspend virus in 1 mL SFEM (set pipette at 500 uL), be careful not to create bubbles.
Transfer all of volume into labeled cryovial, aliquot out 5 microliter into an Eppendorf, and freeze the rest down in -80°C freezer.
Plate 293x cells in a 96 well flat bottom plate at 25,000 cells per well in 100 μL of DMEM 10% FBS.
Add polybrene to the wells such that the final concentration is 10 ug/mL in 100 μL of DMEM 10% FBS.
Plate 2 microliters, 0.2 microliters, and 0.02 microliters of virus for each lentivirus, leaving some blank control wells.
Mix the contents of each well up and down.
Place the plate in a 37°C tissue culture incubator overnight.
Change the media on the 293x-virus titer plate.
Trypsinize cells to detach them, then neutralize with media.
Plate detached cells in a 96 well V bottom plate.
Read out the Vex+ % (AmCyan channel) for different titrations, gating on a blank sample.
Calculate the lentivirus titer using the dilution of virus that leads to a Vex+% between 1-20%.
